logic.indicator: Cutler RSI computed from the last 2 completed close-to-close changes: mean positive change / (mean positive + mean absolute negative); 100 if only gains, 0 if only losses, 50 if both means are zero. Regime SMA includes the signal day close and the prior lookback-1 completed closes.
logic.entry: While flat, after UTC day t is closed, enter long only if Cutler RSI(2) <= entry_rsi and close[t] > SMA(trend_sma_days)[t]. Execute at UTC day t+1 minute-1 open; do not trade on the signal close.
logic.exit: While long, after UTC day t is closed, exit if RSI(2) >= 50 or close[t] <= SMA(trend_sma_days)[t]. Exit takes priority; execute next UTC day minute-1 open. No same-day re-entry.
logic.sizing: Independent 2000 USDT, unlevered long-only spot account; use all available cash for a permitted entry, hold one asset, no transfers or interest. Terminal liquidation at the declared OOS terminal execution.
logic.causality: Signals use only closed UTC daily data available by 00:00 UTC; the next-day execution reference is the 00:01 UTC one-minute open. Prior daily closes used by the SMA/RSI and cost inputs are fully closed before order execution.

parameters.rsi_method: Cutler simple rolling mean (not Wilder recursive smoothing)
parameters.impact_model: 0.5 * sample_stdev(previous 20 complete UTC daily log returns) * sqrt(order quote budget / previous 20 complete UTC daily quote-volume ADV)
parameters.lot_tick_notional: current frozen exchange-info filters; adverse tick rounding and lot floor; 5-minute pre-execution VWAP proxy for percent-price checks
parameters.signal_data: Binance spot one-minute bars, collapsed to completed UTC daily close and quote volume; trade reference is next UTC day 00:01 one-minute open

sources.citation: Zatwarnicki et al. (2023), Effectiveness of the Relative Strength Index Signals in Timing the Cryptocurrency Market, Sensors 23(3):1664, DOI 10.3390/s23031664
sources.use: Motivates testing RSI timing in crypto; does not validate this exact RSI(2), trend filter, costs, or current OOS result.

sources.citation: Turatti, Mendes & Caldeira (2020), Testing for mean reversion in Bitcoin returns with Gibbs-sampling-augmented randomization, Finance Research Letters 34, 101252, DOI 10.1016/j.frl.2019.07.025
sources.use: Finds historical mean aversion in weekly Bitcoin returns in 2010–2019; motivation only, not evidence for the present daily rule.

failure_gates.interpretation: Historical screen only; this repeatedly studied period is not an untouched final holdout or live-profit evidence.
